### Speaker notes

[Timing: 1:30]
Use MOXIE as the concrete example. Start with the observed result shown on the slide: 12 grams of oxygen per hour at the demonstrated high point. Then separate that evidence from the modeled scale-up target of about 34 kilograms per hour and roughly 600 tons over two years.

# Step 10: Publication Bundle - Project ARES-SOE

**Title:** Industrial-Scale Solid Oxide $CO_2$ Electrolysis (SOXE) for Human Mars Missions: A 33.8 kg/hr Modular Architecture for Habitat Life Support and Starship Propellant Refueling

**Author List:** Hypatia AI (Lead Systems Architect), Mars In

### 1. Abstract As human Mars exploration transitions from exploration to habitation, In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) must scale by three orders of magnitude. This paper presents the design and validation framework for Project ARES-SOE (Advanced Regenerative Electrolysis System for Sustained

Oxygen Production), a scaled-up solid-oxide $CO_2$ electrolysis system. Building on the heritage of the NASA MOXIE instrument, the system is designed to produce 592.4 t of $O_2$ over 2 Earth years (17,520 hours)—sufficient to sustain a 12-person habitat and provide 50% of the…

### Speaker notes

[Timing: 1:20]
This slide shows the output of the case study rather than another chat response. The research and engineering folders, publication bundle, diagrams, reports, and other generated work products add up to 145 artifacts in the example.
Emphasize the idea of design control and continuity. The artifacts are indexed to the same problem and can be reviewed, challenged, revised, and passed downstream. The harness can rapidly build a structured feasibility package, but the resulting design is still a proposal until the physical assumptions and tests are validated.

### Speaker notes

Explain why first principles precedes optimization. Inventory laws, measured facts, estimates, habits and opinions. Decompose materials, energy, time, people and money. Every lower bound needs a dated source, units, uncertainty and boundary conditions. A physical minimum differs from a manufacturable estimate and lifecycle cost. Compare a bold and conservative design, then attack each with a falsification test. Keep unknown bounds unknown and never divide by a zero or unknown bound. Deliver assumptions.md, SOURCES.md, cost-gap.csv and a gated 30-day plan. Apply this to oxygen demand, operating hours, energy and degradation in the existing MOXIE scenario. Critical numerical checks retain independent review.

### Speaker notes

The task contract specifies measurable acceptance, input files, scope and limits. Choose one checkable step and record its expected result. File tools return paths, exit status and output streams. Browser tools return observed page state. Connectors return scoped results or errors. ToolReceipt/v1 binds input references, call ID, policy decision, output paths, observations, errors and usage to acceptance checks and RunTrace. PASS requires evidence. FAIL means the criterion is contradicted. BLOCKED names a missing dependency. UNVERIFIED means evidence is insufficient. Repair the affected part within the original time, turn, token and cost caps. Reconcile uncertain external writes before retry. Save progress and continue independent authorized work if another step is blocked. Host isolation, credential proxying and provider connections require their own capability evidence.

6

### Speaker notes

Each specialized harness is a bounded system of role instructions, tools, a working loop, memory access and acceptance tests. Research synthesis and science publish source ledgers, hypotheses, equations, datasets, uncertainties and required tests. Engineering consumes exact approved revisions to produce requirements, trade studies, CAD/geometry, schematics and parts lists, analysis and a verification plan. Project execution consumes the controlled design to produce resources, cost estimates, dependencies, schedules, authorized execution records and field issues. These are selectable stages rather than mandatory extra agents. All stages use the same stable artifact IDs and versioned dependencies. The wiki explains the work, the graph records relationships and the artifact store retains actual bytes. Read and publish through typed manifests. Promote only independently checked outputs within human authority. A stage may use only its approved, relevant context and may not infer extra permissions from store access.
Source: Mars Harness Lab, method 15, Shared Artifact Chain and Correction, 29 October 2026. This is a proposed operating architecture and an illustrative case, not a new MOXIE experiment or a running authenticated cross-application bus. Host tool, storage, permissions, isolation and review enforcement require demonstrated integration.

MARS HARNESS LAB   /   29 OCTOBER 2026

7

### Speaker notes

A downstream issue creates CorrectionRequest/v1 with detector and run, affected artifact revisions, symptom, reproduction, expected result, failing criterion, evidence, severity, root-cause hypothesis, requested upstream deliverable, acceptance check, owner, budget and permission scope. The Director and Memory Steward triage the issue and identify the earliest justified owner. Do not assume every problem requires new science. Preserve the old approved baseline, open a correction branch and mark dependent outputs stale or review-required. Upstream work creates a new immutable revision. Independent review must pass before the minimal affected downstream closure regenerates in dependency order. Recheck interfaces, configurations, tests, plans and approval gates. A workflow revisits stages but each pinned revision graph remains acyclic. Unknown, blocked or failed checks stop dependent promotion. Bounded retries and time/cost caps prevent indefinite repair. Physical work, purchases and external commitments require their own compensation and authorization, not a pretend file rollback. Unrelated branches may continue only with reviewed independence.
Source: Mars Harness Lab, method 15, Shared Artifact Chain and Correction, 29 October 2026. This is a proposed operating architecture and an illustrative case, not a new MOXIE experiment or a running authenticated cross-application bus. Host tool, storage, permissions, isolation and review enforcement require demonstrated integration.

### Speaker notes

[Timing: 1:15]
Governance is what makes automation usable for consequential work. The harness can retrieve and compare sources, draft claims and plans, run approved tools, record outputs, and flag missing or conflicting evidence.
A person must still set the objective and operating limits, approve consequential assumptions, accept evidence and risk, and authorize release or field action. The stop conditions at the bottom are deliberate: stop when a source is missing, evidence conflicts, a tool is out of scope, or authority is unclear.
Update: require explicit policy, redacted tool receipts, capped usage, timeout cancellation and an OS isolation boundary for generated code. Prompt instructions alone do not prove enforcement. Sources: Mars Harness Lab knowledge-workflows.html and conformance.html, release dated 29 October 2026. Concepts synthesized from five user-supplied reference images. Vendor-specific claims and live host capabilities have not been independently verified. No new MOXIE results are claimed.

9

### Speaker notes

At session start read the active task, checkpoint and relevant approved lessons. Use a plan for complex work, including verification steps and a final review. After a correction record scope, root cause, prevention rule and early detection signal. Review skill changes before promotion and preserve supersession. Delegate one bounded assignment per worker only when supported, permitted and justified, using the existing depth, concurrency and parent-budget limits. Before delivery ask what evidence proves completion, what remains uncertain, whether a simpler maintainable solution exists and what fails first. The conformance package maps all 97 assessment requirements and supplies tested local reference utilities. It does not certify runtime enforcement, OS isolation or connected SaaS behavior. ACP and A2A remain deferred. Human authority and nonwaivable safety constraints remain in force.

Open with the full scope of the intelligence layer: science, engineering, build, and operations. Mars systems do not advance one discipline at a time, so the proposed architecture connects them rather than treating AI as a stand-alone assistant.
The thesis is that harnessed agentic AI can help move validated knowledge through design and execution while preserving human judgment, review, and mission responsibility.

### Speaker notes

[Timing: 1:10]
Walk left to right through the evolution. LLM chat can reason and generate, but the result is usually ephemeral. Agentic AI adds tools and multi-step actions. An AI harness adds skills, memory, gates, and repeatability.
The next step is a chain of specialist harnesses for science, engineering, and project management. That chain is what moves AI toward real-world R&D: test, build, and operate. Claude Code and Codex illustrate the middle transition from chat toward a governed engineering worker; this presentation extends the same pattern beyond software.

### Speaker notes

[Timing: 1:05]
The target is to compress the non-physical part of R&D: search, synthesis, documentation, cross-discipline handoffs, change propagation, and review-package creation. The slide contrasts the traditional latency of those activities with the much shorter cycles an automated harness can target.
Keep the qualifier on the slide: this is not about removing humans. Experiments, expert judgment, testing, and approval remain human-governed. The opportunity is to move selected concept-development and documentation loops from long elapsed cycles toward much faster iterations and potentially avoid repeated engineering effort and late discovery of inconsistencies.

Frame Mars as a learning-rate problem. The scarce resource is elapsed time from a mission goal to validated execution. The critical path is science that is good enough to support engineering, engineering that is controlled enough to build, and execution that is authorized and testable.
The agentic harness attacks coordination latency between those stages while preserving the evidence and blockers required to make defensible decisions.

### Speaker notes

[Timing: 1:10]
This is the central design rule: the LLM proposes, but the harness controls what is allowed to become mission state. Models are probabilistic and replaceable. The surrounding process supplies role, identity, instructions, tools, context, memory, specialist agents, skills, guardrails, approval gates, ground truth, work-product contracts, and durable state.
That distinction matters because models will continue to improve. A stable harness lets a stronger future model inherit the same mission-ready skills, evidence rules, contracts, and approval authority instead of rebuilding the operating method from scratch.

### Speaker notes

[Timing: 1:00]
Evidence control prevents a plausible sentence or clean simulation from being mistaken for physical fact. Every claim is labeled by epistemic status: literature, modeled, empirical, or still open.
Promoted claims retain source, scope, assumptions, bounds, method, units, uncertainty, applicability, reviewer, and status. The rule is no silent promotion from one evidence class to another.

The engineering harness begins with approved evidence and turns it into a controlled technical baseline. It develops requirements and constraints, trades architectures and margins, runs design sprints and formal design reviews, applies DFMA and FMEA, defines verification, and then supports launch or operation.

### Speaker notes

A downstream issue creates CorrectionRequest/v1 with detector and run, affected artifact revisions, symptom, reproduction, expected result, failing criterion, evidence, severity, root-cause hypothesis, requested upstream deliverable, acceptance check, owner, budget and permission scope. The Director and Memory Steward triage the issue and identify the earliest justified owner. Do not assume every problem requires new science. Preserve the old approved baseline, open a correction branch and mark dependent outputs stale or review-required. Upstream work creates a new immutable revision. Independent review must pass before the minimal affected downstream closure regenerates in dependency order. Recheck interfaces, configurations, tests, plans and approval gates. A workflow revisits stages but each pinned revision graph remains acyclic. Unknown, blocked or failed checks stop dependent promotion. Bounded retries and time/cost caps prevent indefinite repair. Physical work, purchases and external commitments require their own compensation and authorization, not a pretend file rollback. Unrelated branches may continue only with reviewed independence.
Source: Mars Harness Lab, method 15, Shared Artifact Chain and Correction, 29 October 2026. This is a proposed operating architecture and an illustrative case, not a new MOXIE experiment or a running authenticated cross-application bus. Host tool, storage, permissions, isolation and review enforcement require demonstrated integration.

Ground truth starts with the first claim. The verification chain on the slide ties a claim to its source, requirement, method, result, and current status. A broken link drives rework instead of being hidden.

MARS HARNESS LAB   /   29 OCTOBER 2026

15

### Speaker notes

Every artifact descriptor carries logical ID, immutable revision ID, location and content hash, media type, producer harness/run, exact input revisions, baseline/configuration, evidence class, assumptions, validation status, approvals, owner and timestamps. Use typed relationships such as derived_from, depends_on, implements, verifies, contradicts, blocks and supersedes. raw/ protects original evidence, wiki/ contains curated pages and the index, output/ holds versioned files, ctx/ holds redacted receipts and checkpoints, mem/ contains approved private context. Drafts and stale records never become approved inputs. Stage outputs publish as one coherent manifest transaction with a revision check. Concurrent changes reject the commit and require reconciliation. Reuse unaffected work only with a recorded rationale. Never silently rewrite prior approvals or confuse a JSON approval field with authenticated authority. In the illustrative oxygen-plant example, project planning questions a maintenance assumption, engineering checks it, science investigates lifetime evidence if needed, engineering revises redundancy and project execution recomputes affected spares and schedule. No real reliability or readiness result is claimed.
Source: Mars Harness Lab, method 15, Shared Artifact Chain and Correction, 29 October 2026. This is a proposed operating architecture and an illustrative case, not a new MOXIE experiment or a running authenticated cross-application bus. Host tool, storage, permissions, isolation and review enforcement require demonstrated integration.

### Speaker notes

At session start read the active task, checkpoint and relevant approved lessons. Use a plan for complex work, including verification steps and a final review. After a correction record scope, root cause, prevention rule and early detection signal. Review skill changes before promotion and preserve supersession. Delegate one bounded assignment per worker only when supported, permitted and justified, using the existing depth, concurrency and parent-budget limits. Before delivery ask what evidence proves completion, what remains uncertain, whether a simpler maintainable solution exists and what fails first. The conformance package maps all 97 assessment requirements and supplies tested local reference utilities. It does not certify runtime enforcement, OS isolation or connected SaaS behavior. ACP and A2A remain deferred. Human authority and nonwaivable safety constraints remain in force.
